title: Corrupt Index Remediation and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY Failures
realWorldScenario: A primary key lookup on `orders` where `id = 45910` returns 0 rows. However, `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = 45910` with `SET enable_indexscan = off;` returns the row! The B-tree index is corrupt. A developer ran `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_pkey;` which failed midway after a network timeout.
questionStatement: Explain how B-tree index corruption manifests in PostgreSQL. What state is an index left in when `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY` is interrupted? Detail the safe recovery procedure to rebuild the corrupt primary key index online without locking checkout transactions.

symptoms: Data inconsistency: Index Scan misses existing rows
pg_class shows duplicate or invalid index entries
candidateTasks: Inspect pg_index to verify indisvalid and indisready flags
Explain why idx_orders_pkey_ccnew was left behind by interrupted reindex
Execute safe REINDEX CONCURRENTLY with increased statement_timeout

expectedConcepts: Index corruption causing index scan to miss rows found by sequential scan
REINDEX CONCURRENTLY shadow index naming convention (_ccnew)
Invalid index state (indisvalid = false) causing write amplification
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY to clean up failed index builds
Setting statement_timeout = 0 for heavy maintenance operations
hints: Look for the _ccnew index left behind in the log snippet.
Check pg_index to see why the invalid index is still maintained on writes.
Always disable statement_timeout when running REINDEX on large tables.
